23:1: Surat Al-Mu'minoon In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Razzaq told us, Yunus bin Saleem told me: Yunus bin Yazid Al-Ayli dictated to me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abdul Qari? He said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab say: Whenever the revelation came down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, we could hear near his face the sound of the buzzing of bees. We waited for an hour and then he faced the Qiblah and raised his hands and said: O God, increase us and do not decrease us, honor us and do not humiliate us, give us and do not deprive us, prefer us and do not prefer others over us, be pleased with us and please us. Then he said: Ten verses have been revealed to me, whoever recites them will enter Paradise. Then he recited: The believers have succeeded until he finished the ten. At-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir, and An-Nasa’i in As-Salat from the hadith of Abdul Razzaq with it. At-Tirmidhi said: It is strange, we do not know anyone who narrated it except Yunus bin Saleem, and we do not know Yunus. Al-Nasa'i said in his interpretation: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us, Ja'far told us, on the authority of Abu Imran, on the authority of Yazid ibn Babnous, who said: We said to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers: How was the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur'an. So she recited: "The believers have succeeded" until she reached: "And those who maintain their prayers." She said: This is how the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was. It was narrated on the authority of Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and others: When God created the Garden of Eden and planted it with His own hand, He looked at it and said to it: Speak. It said: "The believers have succeeded." Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Because of the honor He has prepared for them in it. Abu al-'Aliyah said: So God revealed that in His Book. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Mughira bin Salamah told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: God created Paradise as a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and planted it and said to it: Speak. It said: The believers have succeeded. So the angels entered it and it said: Blessed are you, the abode of kings. Then he said: Bishr bin Adam told us, and Yunus bin Ubaidullah Al-Umari told us, Adi bin Al-Fadl told us, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: God created Paradise as a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. Al-Bazzar said: I saw in another place in this hadith the wall of Paradise as a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. So He said to it: Speak. It said: The believers have succeeded. So the angels said: Blessed are you, the abode of kings.” Al-Muluk.” Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know anyone who raised it except Adi bin Al-Fadl, and he is not a hafiz. He is an old man who died early. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali told us, Hisham ibn Khalid told us, Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created the Garden of Eden, He created in it that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: Speak, and it said: ‘The believers have succeeded.’” Baqiyah, on the authority of the Hijazis, is weak. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Munjab ibn al-Harith told us, Hammad ibn Isa al-Absi told us, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, “When God created the Garden of Eden with His hand, and let down its fruits therein, and divided its rivers therein, then He looked at it and said: ‘The believers have succeeded.’ He said: By My glory and majesty, no miser will be my neighbor in you.” Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Kalbi told us, Yaish bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created the Garden of Eden with His hand: a brick of white pearl, a brick of red ruby, and a brick of green emerald. Its mortar is musk, its pebbles are pearls, and its grass is saffron. Then He said to it, ‘Speak.’ It said, ‘The believers have succeeded.’ God said, ‘By My glory and majesty, no miser will be my neighbor in you.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.’” God the Almighty says: The believers have succeeded meaning they have won, been happy and achieved success. They are the believers who are described by these attributes. Who are humble in their prayers. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Humble means fearful and calm. This was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Al-Zuhri. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: Humility is humility of the heart. This was also narrated by Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their gaze and lowered their wings. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: The companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to raise their gaze to the sky in prayer. When this verse was revealed: The believers have succeeded * Who are humble in their prayers they lowered their gaze to the place of their prostration. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: They used to say: He should not let his gaze go beyond his prayer place. If he is accustomed to looking, then he should close it. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Then Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority and on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah also, without a chain of transmission, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do that until this verse was revealed. Humility in prayer is only achieved by the one who empties his heart for it and is occupied with it from everything else and prefers it over everything else. Then it will be a comfort for him and a delight to his eyes, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Perfume and women have been made beloved to me, and the delight of my eyes has been made in prayer. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Mus`ar narrated to us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of a man from Aslam, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Bilal, give us rest with prayer. Imam Ahmad also said: `Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of `Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: I entered with my father upon our brother-in-law from the Ansar, and the time for prayer came, so he said: O girl, bring me water for ablution so that I may pray and rest. He saw that we disapproved of that, so he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Get up, O Bilal, and give us rest with prayer. His statement: And those who turn away from ill speech means from falsehood, and it includes polytheism as some of them said, and sins as others said, and what is of no benefit in words and actions, as God Almighty said: And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity. Qatada said: By God, God’s command came to them that which stopped them from that. And his saying: And those who are doers of zakat Most of them are of the opinion that what is meant by zakat here is zakat on wealth, even though this verse is Meccan, and zakat was only imposed in Medina in the second year of the Hijra. It appears that what was imposed in Medina is the one with the specific zakat and amounts. Otherwise, it appears that the origin of zakat was obligatory in Mecca, as God Almighty said in Surat Al-An’am, which is Meccan: And give its due on the day of its harvest. It may be possible that what is meant by zakat here is zakat of the soul from polytheism and impurity, like His saying: He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it with corruption. And like His saying: And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakat, according to one of the two opinions in their interpretation. It may be possible that both matters are meant, which are zakat of souls and zakat of wealth, because they are part of zakat of souls, and the complete believer is the one who does this and that, and God knows best. And His statement, “And those who guard their private parts, Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.” That is, those who have guarded their private parts from what is forbidden, so they do not fall into what God has forbidden them from of adultery and sodomy. They do not approach anyone except their wives whom God has made lawful for them or those their right hands possess of concubines. And whoever engages in what God has made lawful for him, then there is no blame upon him nor is there any blame upon him. For this reason He said, “Then they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that,” that is, other than wives and female slaves, then those are the transgressors, that is, the aggressors. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that a woman took her slave and said: I have interpreted a verse from the Book of God, or what their right hands possess. So she was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have interpreted a verse from the Book of God, the Almighty, in a way other than its meaning. He said: So he struck the slave and cut off his head, and said: After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim. This is a strange, disconnected report, mentioned by Ibn Jarir in his interpretation of the beginning of Surat al-Ma’idah, and it is more appropriate here. He only forbade her to men in order to treat her with the opposite of what she intended, and God knows best. Imam Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him, based their evidence for the prohibition of masturbation on this noble verse: And those who guard their private parts * Except from their wives or those their right hands possess. He said: This action is outside of these two categories, and God Almighty said: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. They relied on a hadith narrated by Imam Al-Hasan bin Arafa in his famous section where he said: Ali bin Thabit Al-Jazari told me on the authority of Muslimah bin Ja’far on the authority of Hassan bin Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are seven whom God will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He gather them with the worlds, and He will admit them to Hellfire as the first to enter unless they repent. And whoever repents, God will accept his repentance: the one who fornicates with his hand, the one who does it and the one it is done to, the alcoholic, the one who beats his parents until they call for help, the one who harms his neighbors until they curse him, and the one who fornicates with his neighbor’s wife.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission includes someone who is not known due to his ignorance, and God Know. And His statement: And those who are to their trusts and covenants attentive means that if they are entrusted with something, they do not betray it, but rather return it to its people, and if they make a covenant or agreement, they fulfill it, unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites about whom the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And His statement: And those who maintain their prayers means they are consistent in performing them at their appointed times, as Ibn Mas’ud said: “I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, which deed is most beloved to God? He said: Prayer at its appointed time. I said: Then which? He said: Kindness to parents. I said: Then which? He said: Jihad in the cause of God.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in Al-Bukhari and Muslim. And in Al-Mustadrak Al-Hakim, he said: Prayer at the beginning of its appointed time. Ibn Masoud and Masrooq said about His statement: And those who maintain their prayers meaning the times of prayer. This is what Abu Ad-Dahha, Alqamah bin Qais, Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said. Qatada said: On its times, bowing and prostrating. God began mentioning these praiseworthy qualities with prayer and concluded it with prayer, thus indicating its superiority, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Be upright and you will never be able to count them. Know that the best of your deeds is prayer. And none maintains ablution except a believer.” And when God described them as having these praiseworthy qualities and righteous deeds, He said: Those are the inheritors * Who will inherit Paradise; they will abide therein eternally. It is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Paradise, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is none among you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. If he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise will inherit his home. This is what He said: ‘Those are the inheritors.’” Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Those are the inheritors. He said: There is none among you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. As for the believer, he builds his home in Paradise and demolishes his home in Hell. As for the disbeliever, he demolishes his home in Paradise and builds his home in Hell. It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair something similar to this, that the believers inherit the homes of the infidels because they were created to worship God Almighty alone, with no partner for Him. So when these believers did what was required of them in worship, and those left what they were commanded to do for which they were created, these people attained the share of those who had obeyed their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and even more so, and this is what was proven in Saheeh Muslim on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, people from the Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and God will forgive them and place them on the Jews and Christians. And in another version of his: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: This is your release from the Fire.” So Umar bin Abdul Aziz made Abu Burdah swear by God, there is no god but Him, three times, that his father told him about that on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So he swore to him. I said: This verse is like the saying of God Almighty: That is the Paradise which We shall inherit from those of Our servants who were righteous and like His saying: And that is the Paradise. Which you have inherited because of what you used to do. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said, Paradise in Roman is Al-Firdaws. Some of the Salaf said: The garden is not called Al-Firdaws unless it has grapes in it. And God knows best.

He said: So he struck the slave and cut off his head, and said: After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim. He said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab say: Whenever the revelation came down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, we could hear near his face something like the buzzing of bees. We waited for an hour and then he faced the Qiblah and raised his hands and said: "O God, increase us and do not decrease us, honor us and do not humiliate us, give us and do not deprive us, prefer us and do not prefer others over us, be pleased with us and please us - then he said: Ten verses have been revealed to me, whoever recites them will enter Paradise." Then he recited: The believers have succeeded until he finished the ten. She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur'an. So she recited: The believers have succeeded until she reached: And those who maintain their prayers. She said: This is how the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was. It was narrated on the authority of Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and others: When God created the Garden of Eden and planted it with His own hand, He looked at it and said to it: Speak. It said: The believers have succeeded. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Because of the honor He has prepared for them in it. Abu al-'Aliyah said: So God revealed that in His Book. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Mughira bin Salamah told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: God created Paradise as a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and planted it and said to it: Speak. It said: The believers have succeeded. So the angels entered it and it said: Blessed are you, the abode of kings. Then he said: Bishr bin Adam told us, and Yunus bin Ubaidullah Al-Umari told us, Adi bin Al-Fadl told us, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: God created Paradise as a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. Al-Bazzar said: I saw in another place in this hadith the wall of Paradise as a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and its mortar is musk. So He said to it: Speak. It said: The believers have succeeded. So the angels said: Blessed are you, the abode of kings.” Al-Muluk.” Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know anyone who raised it except Adi bin Al-Fadl, and he is not a hafiz. He is an old man who died early. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali told us, Hisham ibn Khalid told us, Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created the Garden of Eden, He created in it that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: Speak, and it said: ‘The believers have succeeded.’” Baqiyah, on the authority of the Hijazis, is weak. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Munjab ibn al-Harith told us, Hammad ibn Isa al-Absi told us, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, “When God created the Garden of Eden with His hand, and let down its fruits therein, and divided its rivers therein, then He looked at it and said: ‘The believers have succeeded.’ He said: By My glory and majesty, no miser will be my neighbor in you.” Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Kalbi told us, Yaish bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created the Garden of Eden with His hand: a brick of white pearl, a brick of red ruby, and a brick of green emerald. Its mortar is musk, its pebbles are pearls, and its grass is saffron. Then He said to it, ‘Speak.’ It said, ‘The believers have succeeded.’ God said, ‘By My glory and majesty, no miser will be my neighbor in you.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.’” God the Almighty says: The believers have succeeded meaning they have won, been happy and achieved success. They are the believers who are described by these attributes. Who are humble in their prayers. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Humble means fearful and calm. This was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Al-Zuhri. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: Humility is humility of the heart. This was also narrated by Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their gaze and lowered their wings. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: The companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to raise their gaze to the sky in prayer. When this verse was revealed: The believers have succeeded * Who are humble in their prayers they lowered their gaze to the place of their prostration. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: They used to say: He should not let his gaze go beyond his prayer place. If he is accustomed to looking, then he should close it. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Then Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority and on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah also, without a chain of transmission, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do that until this verse was revealed. Humility in prayer is only achieved by the one who empties his heart for it and is occupied with it from everything else and prefers it over everything else. Then it will be a comfort for him and a delight to his eyes, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Perfume and women have been made beloved to me, and the delight of my eyes has been made in prayer. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Mus`ar narrated to us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of a man from Aslam, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Bilal, give us rest with prayer. Imam Ahmad also said: `Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of `Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: I entered with my father upon our brother-in-law from the Ansar, and the time for prayer came, so he said: O girl, bring me water for ablution so that I may pray and rest. He saw that we disapproved of that, so he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Get up, O Bilal, and give us rest with prayer. His statement: And those who turn away from ill speech means from falsehood, and it includes polytheism as some of them said, and sins as others said, and what is of no benefit in words and actions, as God Almighty said: And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity. Qatada said: By God, God’s command came to them that which stopped them from that. And his saying: And those who are doers of zakat Most of them are of the opinion that what is meant by zakat here is zakat on wealth, even though this verse is Meccan, and zakat was only imposed in Medina in the second year of the Hijra. It appears that what was imposed in Medina is the one with the specific zakat and amounts. Otherwise, it appears that the origin of zakat was obligatory in Mecca, as God Almighty said in Surat Al-An’am, which is Meccan: And give its due on the day of its harvest. It may be possible that what is meant by zakat here is zakat of the soul from polytheism and impurity, like His saying: He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it with corruption. And like His saying: And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakat, according to one of the two opinions in their interpretation. It may be possible that both matters are meant, which are zakat of souls and zakat of wealth, because they are part of zakat of souls, and the complete believer is the one who does this and that, and God knows best. And His statement, “And those who guard their private parts, Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.” That is, those who have guarded their private parts from what is forbidden, so they do not fall into what God has forbidden them from of adultery and sodomy. They do not approach anyone except their wives whom God has made lawful for them or those their right hands possess of concubines. And whoever engages in what God has made lawful for him, then there is no blame upon him nor is there any blame upon him. For this reason He said, “Then they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that,” that is, other than wives and female slaves, then those are the transgressors, that is, the aggressors. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that a woman took her slave and said: I have interpreted a verse from the Book of God, or what their right hands possess. So she was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have interpreted a verse from the Book of God, the Almighty, in a way other than its meaning. He said: So he struck the slave and cut off his head, and said: After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim. This is a strange, disconnected report, mentioned by Ibn Jarir in his interpretation of the beginning of Surat al-Ma’idah, and it is more appropriate here. He only forbade her to men in order to treat her with the opposite of what she intended, and God knows best. Imam Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him, based their evidence for the prohibition of masturbation on this noble verse: And those who guard their private parts * Except from their wives or those their right hands possess. He said: This action is outside of these two categories, and God Almighty said: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. They relied on a hadith narrated by Imam Al-Hasan bin Arafa in his famous section where he said: Ali bin Thabit Al-Jazari told me on the authority of Muslimah bin Ja’far on the authority of Hassan bin Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are seven whom God will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He gather them with the worlds, and He will admit them to Hellfire as the first to enter unless they repent. And whoever repents, God will accept his repentance: the one who fornicates with his hand, the one who does it and the one it is done to, the alcoholic, the one who beats his parents until they call for help, the one who harms his neighbors until they curse him, and the one who fornicates with his neighbor’s wife.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission includes someone who is not known due to his ignorance, and God Know. And His statement: And those who are to their trusts and covenants attentive means that if they are entrusted with something, they do not betray it, but rather return it to its people, and if they make a covenant or agreement, they fulfill it, unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites about whom the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And His statement: And those who maintain their prayers means they are consistent in performing them at their appointed times, as Ibn Mas’ud said: “I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, which deed is most beloved to God? He said: Prayer at its appointed time. I said: Then which? He said: Kindness to parents. I said: Then which? He said: Jihad in the cause of God.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in Al-Bukhari and Muslim. And in Al-Mustadrak Al-Hakim, he said: Prayer at the beginning of its appointed time. Ibn Masoud and Masrooq said about His statement: And those who maintain their prayers meaning the times of prayer. This is what Abu Ad-Dahha, Alqamah bin Qais, Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said. Qatada said: On its times, bowing and prostrating. God began mentioning these praiseworthy qualities with prayer and concluded it with prayer, thus indicating its superiority, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Be upright and you will never be able to count them. Know that the best of your deeds is prayer. And none maintains ablution except a believer.” And when God described them as having these praiseworthy qualities and righteous deeds, He said: Those are the inheritors * Who will inherit Paradise; they will abide therein eternally. It is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Paradise, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is none among you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. If he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise will inherit his home. This is what He said: ‘Those are the inheritors.’” Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Those are the inheritors. He said: There is none among you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. As for the believer, he builds his home in Paradise and demolishes his home in Hell. As for the disbeliever, he demolishes his home in Paradise and builds his home in Hell. It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair something similar to this, that the believers inherit the homes of the infidels because they were created to worship God Almighty alone, with no partner for Him. So when these believers did what was required of them in worship, and those left what they were commanded to do for which they were created, these people attained the share of those who had obeyed their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and even more so, and this is what was proven in Saheeh Muslim on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, people from the Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and God will forgive them and place them on the Jews and Christians. And in another version of his: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: This is your release from the Fire.” So Umar bin Abdul Aziz made Abu Burdah swear by God, there is no god but Him, three times, that his father told him about that on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So he swore to him. I said: This verse is like the saying of God Almighty: That is the Paradise which We shall inherit from those of Our servants who were righteous and like His saying: And that is the Paradise. Which you have inherited because of what you used to do. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said, Paradise in Roman is Al-Firdaws. Some of the Salaf said: The garden is not called Al-Firdaws unless it has grapes in it. And God knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: `Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of `Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: I entered with my father upon our brother-in-law from the Ansar, and the time for prayer came, so he said: O girl, bring me water for ablution so that I may pray and rest. He saw that we disapproved of that, so he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Get up, O Bilal, and give us rest with prayer. His statement: And those who turn away from ill speech means from falsehood, and it includes polytheism as some of them said, and sins as others said, and what is of no benefit in words and actions, as God Almighty said: And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity. Qatada said: By God, God’s command came to them that which stopped them from that. And his saying: And those who are doers of zakat Most of them are of the opinion that what is meant by zakat here is zakat on wealth, even though this verse is Meccan, and zakat was only imposed in Medina in the second year of the Hijra. It appears that what was imposed in Medina is the one with the specific zakat and amounts. Otherwise, it appears that the origin of zakat was obligatory in Mecca, as God Almighty said in Surat Al-An’am, which is Meccan: And give its due on the day of its harvest. It may be possible that what is meant by zakat here is zakat of the soul from polytheism and impurity, like His saying: He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it with corruption. And like His saying: And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakat, according to one of the two opinions in their interpretation. It may be possible that both matters are meant, which are zakat of souls and zakat of wealth, because they are part of zakat of souls, and the complete believer is the one who does this and that, and God knows best. And His statement, “And those who guard their private parts, Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.” That is, those who have guarded their private parts from what is forbidden, so they do not fall into what God has forbidden them from of adultery and sodomy. They do not approach anyone except their wives whom God has made lawful for them or those their right hands possess of concubines. And whoever engages in what God has made lawful for him, then there is no blame upon him nor is there any blame upon him. For this reason He said, “Then they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that,” that is, other than wives and female slaves, then those are the transgressors, that is, the aggressors. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that a woman took her slave and said: I have interpreted a verse from the Book of God, or what their right hands possess. So she was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have interpreted a verse from the Book of God, the Almighty, in a way other than its meaning. He said: So he struck the slave and cut off his head, and said: After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim. This is a strange, disconnected report, mentioned by Ibn Jarir in his interpretation of the beginning of Surat al-Ma’idah, and it is more appropriate here. He only forbade her to men in order to treat her with the opposite of what she intended, and God knows best. Imam Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him, based their evidence for the prohibition of masturbation on this noble verse: And those who guard their private parts * Except from their wives or those their right hands possess. He said: This action is outside of these two categories, and God Almighty said: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. They relied on a hadith narrated by Imam Al-Hasan bin Arafa in his famous section where he said: Ali bin Thabit Al-Jazari told me on the authority of Muslimah bin Ja’far on the authority of Hassan bin Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are seven whom God will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He gather them with the worlds, and He will admit them to Hellfire as the first to enter unless they repent. And whoever repents, God will accept his repentance: the one who fornicates with his hand, the one who does it and the one it is done to, the alcoholic, the one who beats his parents until they call for help, the one who harms his neighbors until they curse him, and the one who fornicates with his neighbor’s wife.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission includes someone who is not known due to his ignorance, and God Know. And His statement: And those who are to their trusts and covenants attentive means that if they are entrusted with something, they do not betray it, but rather return it to its people, and if they make a covenant or agreement, they fulfill it, unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites about whom the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And His statement: And those who maintain their prayers means they are consistent in performing them at their appointed times, as Ibn Mas’ud said: “I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, which deed is most beloved to God? He said: Prayer at its appointed time. I said: Then which? He said: Kindness to parents. I said: Then which? He said: Jihad in the cause of God.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in Al-Bukhari and Muslim. And in Al-Mustadrak Al-Hakim, he said: Prayer at the beginning of its appointed time. Ibn Masoud and Masrooq said about His statement: And those who maintain their prayers meaning the times of prayer. This is what Abu Ad-Dahha, Alqamah bin Qais, Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said. Qatada said: On its times, bowing and prostrating. God began mentioning these praiseworthy qualities with prayer and concluded it with prayer, thus indicating its superiority, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Be upright and you will never be able to count them. Know that the best of your deeds is prayer. And none maintains ablution except a believer.” And when God described them as having these praiseworthy qualities and righteous deeds, He said: Those are the inheritors * Who will inherit Paradise; they will abide therein eternally. It is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Paradise, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is none among you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. If he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise will inherit his home. This is what He said: ‘Those are the inheritors.’” Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Those are the inheritors. He said: There is none among you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. As for the believer, he builds his home in Paradise and demolishes his home in Hell. As for the disbeliever, he demolishes his home in Paradise and builds his home in Hell. It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair something similar to this, that the believers inherit the homes of the infidels because they were created to worship God Almighty alone, with no partner for Him. So when these believers did what was required of them in worship, and those left what they were commanded to do for which they were created, these people attained the share of those who had obeyed their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and even more so, and this is what was proven in Saheeh Muslim on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, people from the Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and God will forgive them and place them on the Jews and Christians. And in another version of his: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and it will be said: This is your release from the Fire.” So Umar bin Abdul Aziz made Abu Burdah swear by God, there is no god but Him, three times, that his father told him about that on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So he swore to him. I said: This verse is like the saying of God Almighty: That is the Paradise which We shall inherit from those of Our servants who were righteous and like His saying: And that is the Paradise. Which you have inherited because of what you used to do. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said, Paradise in Roman is Al-Firdaws. Some of the Salaf said: The garden is not called Al-Firdaws unless it has grapes in it. And God knows best.
23:12: The Almighty says, informing about the beginning of the creation of man from a lineage of clay, and he is Adam, peace be upon him, whom God created from clay from altered black mud. Al-A'mash said on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr on the authority of Abu Yahya on the authority of Ibn Abbas, from a lineage of clay he said: from the cream of water. Mujahid said: from a lineage, meaning from the semen of Adam. Ibn Jarir said: Adam was called clay because he was created from it. Qatada said: Adam was extracted from clay, and this is clearer in meaning and closer to the context, for Adam, peace be upon him, was created from sticky clay, which is the clay from altered black mud, and he was created from dust as the Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then suddenly you are human beings dispersing. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Usama bin Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God created Adam from a handful that He took from all the earth, and the children of Adam came according to the earth, and among them came the red, the white, the black, and those in between, and the wicked, the good, and those in between.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Awf al-A’rabi, with a similar wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. Then We made him a sperm-drop. This pronoun refers to the human race, as He said in the other verse: “And He began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his offspring from an extract of despised water.” That is, weak, as He said: Did We not create you from a despised water? Then We placed him in a firm lodging. That is, the womb prepared for that and ready for him. “For a known measure. So We measured, and excellent are We in measuring.” That is, for a known period and a specific term until it was perfected and moved from one state to another and one characteristic to another. That is why He said here: Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot. That is, then We made the sperm-drop, which is the gushing water that comes out of the man’s loins, which is his back, and the woman’s collarbones, which are the bones of her chest between the collarbone and the navel, so it became a red clot in the shape of an oblong clot. Ikrimah said: It is blood. Then We made the clot into a lump of flesh. That is, a piece like a piece of flesh with no shape or outline. Then We made the lump of flesh into bones. That is, We formed it with a head, two hands, and two feet. With its bones, nerves and veins. Others read: Then We created the lump of flesh into bones. Ibn Abbas said: It is the back bone. In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every body of the son of Adam decays except the coccyx, from which he was created and from which he will be reconstructed. “Then We covered the bones with flesh,” meaning, and made something to cover it, strengthen it, and make it stronger. Then We produced him as another creation, meaning, then We breathed the soul into him, so he moved and became another creation with hearing, sight, perception, movement, and agitation. So blessed be God, the best of creators. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Jaafar bin Musafir told us, Yahya bin Hassan told us, Al-Nadr told us, meaning Ibn Kathir, the client of Banu Hashim, told us, Zaid bin Ali told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the sperm grows for four months, God sends an angel to it and he breathes the spirit into it in three layers of darkness. This is what He said: Then We produced him as another creation, meaning We breathed the spirit into him. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that he breathed the spirit. Ibn Abbas said: Then We produced him as another creation, meaning We breathed the spirit into him. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Dahhak, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Zaid said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then We produced him as another creation, meaning that We moved him from one state to another until he emerged as a baby, then grew up as a child, then had a wet dream, then became a young man, then an adult, then an old man, then decrepit. And Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said something similar to that, and there is no contradiction, because from the beginning of the breathing of the soul into him, these movements and states began, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him - he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he is the truthful and believed one, told us: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop of semen, then he is a clot for a similar period, then he is a lump of flesh for a similar period, then an angel is sent to him who breathes the spirit into him and he is commanded with four words: his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy. By the One besides Whom there is no god, one of you may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the Book will overtake him and he will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Hell and he will enter it. And one of you may do the deeds of the people of Hell until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the Book will overtake him and he will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise and he will enter it.” They both reported it from the hadith of Sulayman bin Mihran Al-A’mash. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, who said: Abdullah - meaning Ibn Masoud - said: When the sperm falls into the womb, it flies into every hair and nail, and remains for forty days, then returns to the womb and becomes a clot. Imam Ahmad also said: Hussain ibn Al-Hasan told us, Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was speaking to his companions, and the Quraysh said: O Jew, this one claims to be a prophet. He said: I will ask him about something that only a prophet knows. He said: “So he came to him and sat down, and said: O Muhammad, from what is man created?” He said: O Jew, from each is created: from the sperm of the man and from the sperm of the woman. As for the sperm of the man, it is a thick sperm from which are the bones and nerves, and as for the sperm of the woman, it is a thin sperm from which are the flesh and blood.” He said: Thus did those before you say. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The angel enters upon the sperm after it has settled in the womb for forty nights, and says: O Lord, what? Will it be wretched or happy, male or female? God says, and they write it down, and his deeds, his traces, his misfortune, and his provision are written down, then the scroll is folded up and nothing is added to what is in it nor is anything subtracted from it.” Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, who is Ibn Dinar, with a similar chain of transmission, and from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, Amir ibn Wathilah, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid Abu Sarihah al-Ghifari with a similar chain of transmission, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ahmad bin Abdah told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Ubaidullah bin Abi Bakr told us on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has assigned an angel to the womb, and he says: ‘O Lord, a sperm-drop, O Lord, a clot, O Lord, a lump of flesh.’ So when God wants to create it, he says: ‘O Lord, male or female? Wretched or happy? What is the provision and the life span?’ He said: ‘That is written in the womb of its mother.’” They included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid on his authority. And His saying: So blessed be God, the best of creators, meaning when He mentioned His power and kindness in creating this sperm from one state to another and from one form to another until it became what it became of a perfect, well-formed human being, He said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib told us, Abu Dawud told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Ali ibn Zayd told us on the authority of Anas who said: Umar, meaning Ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: I agreed with my Lord and He agreed with me in four things: This verse was revealed: And We created man from an extract of clay, the verse. I said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. So the verse was revealed: So blessed be God, the best of creators. He also said: My father told us, Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Jabir al-Ju'fi, on the authority of Amer al-Sha'bi, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dictated this verse to me: "And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot, then We made the clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump of flesh into bones, then We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation." Mu'adh said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed, so Mu'adh said to him: Why are you laughing, O Messenger of God? He said: "With it it ends. So blessed be God, the best of creators." In the chain of transmission of Jabir bin Yazid al-Ju'fi is very weak, and in this report of his there is a great objection, because this surah is Meccan, and Zaid bin Thabit only wrote the revelation in Medina, and likewise the conversion of Mu'adh bin Jabal to Islam was also in Medina, and God knows best. And His statement: Then after that you will die means after this first creation from nothingness you will go to death. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected meaning the last creation. Then God will create the last creation meaning the Day of Resurrection and the resurrection of the souls to the bodies, and He will hold the creation to account, and every worker will be fully compensated for his work, if it was good then good and if it was evil then evil.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, who said: Abdullah - meaning Ibn Masoud - said: When the sperm falls into the womb, it flies into every hair and nail, and remains for forty days, then returns to the womb and becomes a clot. Imam Ahmad also said: Hussain ibn Al-Hasan told us, Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was speaking to his companions, and the Quraysh said: O Jew, this one claims to be a prophet. He said: I will ask him about something that only a prophet knows. He said: “So he came to him and sat down, and said: O Muhammad, from what is man created?” He said: O Jew, from each is created: from the sperm of the man and from the sperm of the woman. As for the sperm of the man, it is a thick sperm from which are the bones and nerves, and as for the sperm of the woman, it is a thin sperm from which are the flesh and blood.” He said: Thus did those before you say. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The angel enters upon the sperm after it has settled in the womb for forty nights, and says: O Lord, what? Will it be wretched or happy, male or female? God says, and they write it down, and his deeds, his traces, his misfortune, and his provision are written down, then the scroll is folded up and nothing is added to what is in it nor is anything subtracted from it.” Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, who is Ibn Dinar, with a similar chain of transmission, and from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, Amir ibn Wathilah, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid Abu Sarihah al-Ghifari with a similar chain of transmission, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ahmad bin Abdah told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Ubaidullah bin Abi Bakr told us on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has assigned an angel to the womb, and he says: ‘O Lord, a sperm-drop, O Lord, a clot, O Lord, a lump of flesh.’ So when God wants to create it, he says: ‘O Lord, male or female? Wretched or happy? What is the provision and the life span?’ He said: ‘That is written in the womb of its mother.’” They included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid on his authority. And His saying: So blessed be God, the best of creators, meaning when He mentioned His power and kindness in creating this sperm from one state to another and from one form to another until it became what it became of a perfect, well-formed human being, He said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib told us, Abu Dawud told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Ali ibn Zayd told us on the authority of Anas who said: Umar, meaning Ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: I agreed with my Lord and He agreed with me in four things: This verse was revealed: And We created man from an extract of clay, the verse. I said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. So the verse was revealed: So blessed be God, the best of creators. He also said: My father told us, Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Jabir al-Ju'fi, on the authority of Amer al-Sha'bi, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dictated this verse to me: "And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot, then We made the clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump of flesh into bones, then We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation." Mu'adh said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed, so Mu'adh said to him: Why are you laughing, O Messenger of God? He said: "With it it ends. So blessed be God, the best of creators." In the chain of transmission of Jabir bin Yazid al-Ju'fi is very weak, and in this report of his there is a great objection, because this surah is Meccan, and Zaid bin Thabit only wrote the revelation in Medina, and likewise the conversion of Mu'adh bin Jabal to Islam was also in Medina, and God knows best. And His statement: Then after that you will die means after this first creation from nothingness you will go to death. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected meaning the last creation. Then God will create the last creation meaning the Day of Resurrection and the resurrection of the souls to the bodies, and He will hold the creation to account, and every worker will be fully compensated for his work, if it was good then good and if it was evil then evil.
23:17: When God Almighty mentioned the creation of man, He followed it up with mentioning the creation of the seven heavens. God Almighty often mentions the creation of the heavens and the earth with the creation of man, as He Almighty said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. And so it is at the beginning of Alif, Lam, Meem the prostration that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite on Friday morning. At the beginning of it is the creation of the heavens and the earth, then a statement of the creation of man from a lineage of clay, and in it is the matter of resurrection and reward and other purposes. And His saying: Seven paths Mujahid said: He means the seven heavens, and this is like the saying of God Almighty: The seven heavens glorify Him and the earth and whoever is in them “Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers” “God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends between them so that you may know that God is over all things competent and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge” and thus He said here And We have certainly created above you seven paths and We are not unaware of creation meaning He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends in it, and He is with you wherever you are and God is Seeing of what you do, and He, glory be to Him, does not hide from Him a sky by a sky nor an earth by an earth, nor a mountain but He knows what is in its ruggedness, nor a sea but He knows what is in its depths. He knows the number of what is in the mountains, hills, sands, seas, deserts and trees And not a leaf falls but He knows it, and no grain is there in the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is in a clear book
23:18: The Almighty mentions His countless blessings upon His servants in sending down rain from the sky in proportion, that is, according to need, not too much so that it spoils the land and the civilization, nor too little so that it is not sufficient for the crops and fruits, but rather according to the need for it for irrigation, drinking and benefit from it, so that the lands that need a lot of water for their cultivation and whose dung cannot bear the rain falling on them, water is brought to them from other lands as in the land of Egypt and it is called the barren land, God brings to it the water of the Nile with red clay that it sweeps from the land of Abyssinia during the time of its rains, so the water comes carrying red clay and irrigates the land of Egypt and settles the clay on their land for them to plant in it, because their land is salt marshland mostly sandy, so glory be to the Gracious, the All-Knowing, the Merciful, the Forgiving. His saying: And We caused it to settle in the earth means that We made the water, when it descends from the clouds, remain in the earth, and We made the earth receptive to it, so that it would drink it and nourish the grains and seeds in it. And His statement: And indeed, We are able to take it away means, if We willed that it not rain, We would have done so. If We willed, We would have diverted it from you to salt marshes, wildernesses, and wastelands. We would have done so. If We willed, We would have made it brackish, so that it would not be of benefit to drink or give to drink, We would have done so. If We willed, We would have made it not descend into the earth, but rather flow over its surface, We would have done so. If We willed, We would have made it, when it descends into it, sink to a level that you would not reach or benefit from, We would have done so. But by His kindness and mercy, He sends down water upon you from the clouds, sweet, fresh, and clear. He makes it settle in the earth and makes it flow as springs in the earth, opening springs and rivers and watering crops and fruits with it. You and your animals and livestock drink from it, and you wash from it and purify yourselves from it and clean yourselves. So to Him is praise and thanks. And His statement: Then We produced for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines means: We brought forth for you, by what We sent down from the sky, gardens, meaning orchards and gardens, of delight, meaning of a beautiful view. And His statement: of palm trees and grapevines means in them are palm trees and grapevines, and this is what the people of the Hijaz were accustomed to, and there is no difference between one thing and its counterpart. And likewise with regard to every people of a region who have fruits from the blessings of God upon them that they are unable to thank Him for. And His statement: For you therein are many fruits, meaning of all fruits, as He said: He causes to grow for you thereby crops and olives and palm trees and grapevines and of all fruits. And His statement: And from them you eat is as if it is conjoined with something understood, the meaning of which is that you look at its beauty and ripeness and from it you eat. His saying: And a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai means the olive tree, and Mount is the mountain. Some of them said: It is only called Mount if it has trees, but if it is devoid of them, it is called a mountain, not Mount. And God knows best. Mount Sinai is Mount Sinin, and it is the mountain on which God spoke to Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, and the mountains around it that have olive trees. And his saying: It grows with oil. Some of them said: The letter ba is redundant, and its meaning is that it grows with oil as in the Arabs’ saying: So-and-so threw his hand, meaning his hand. As for the saying of those who include the action, its meaning is that it comes out with oil or comes with oil. For this reason he said: And dye meaning it makes it dark, as Qatadah said, For the eaters meaning in it is what is beneficial from oil and dyeing, as Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’ on the authority of Abdullah bin Isa on the authority of Ata’ al-Shami, on the authority of Abu Asid, whose name is Malik bin Rabi’ah al-Sa’idi al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eat oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it is from a blessed tree. Abd bin Hamid said in his Musnad and Tafsir: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eat olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it comes from a blessed tree. At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from more than one source on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. At-Tirmidhi said: It is not known except from his hadith, and he was confused in it, for he might mention Umar in it, and sometimes he did not mention him. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Al-Sa’b bin Hakim bin Sharik bin Numailah told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: I hosted Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the night of Ashura, and he fed me from the head of a cold camel, and he fed us oil, and he said: This is the blessed oil that God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: “And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you therein are many benefits, and from them you eat. And on them and on ships you are carried.” The Almighty mentions the benefits He has made for His creation in livestock, and that is that they drink from their milk that comes out from between excrement and blood, and they eat from their lambs and wear from their wool, fur and hair, and ride on their backs, and carry heavy loads from them to lands far from them, as the Almighty said: “And they carry your loads to a land which you could not have reached except with difficulty. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.” And the Almighty said: “Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, so they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat. And for them therein are benefits and drinks. So will they not be grateful?”

At-Tirmidhi said: It is not known except from his hadith, and he was confused in it, for he might mention Umar in it, and sometimes he did not mention him. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Al-Sa’b bin Hakim bin Sharik bin Numailah told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: I hosted Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the night of Ashura, and he fed me from the head of a cold camel, and he fed us oil, and he said: This is the blessed oil that God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: “And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you therein are many benefits, and from them you eat. His saying: And We caused it to settle in the earth means that We made the water, when it descends from the clouds, remain in the earth, and We made the earth receptive to it, so that it would drink it and nourish the grains and seeds in it. And His statement: And indeed, We are able to take it away means, if We willed that it not rain, We would have done so. If We willed, We would have diverted it from you to salt marshes, wildernesses, and wastelands. We would have done so. If We willed, We would have made it brackish, so that it would not be of benefit to drink or give to drink, We would have done so. If We willed, We would have made it not descend into the earth, but rather flow over its surface, We would have done so. If We willed, We would have made it, when it descends into it, sink to a level that you would not reach or benefit from, We would have done so. But by His kindness and mercy, He sends down water upon you from the clouds, sweet, fresh, and clear. He makes it settle in the earth and makes it flow as springs in the earth, opening springs and rivers and watering crops and fruits with it. You and your animals and livestock drink from it, and you wash from it and purify yourselves from it and clean yourselves. So to Him is praise and thanks. And likewise with regard to every people of a region who have fruits from the blessings of God upon them that they are unable to thank Him for. And His statement: For you therein are many fruits, meaning of all fruits, as He said: He causes to grow for you thereby crops and olives and palm trees and grapevines and of all fruits. Some of them said: It is only called Mount if it has trees, but if it is devoid of them, it is called a mountain, not Mount. And God knows best. 23:23: God Almighty tells about Noah, peace be upon him, when He sent him to his people to warn them of God's punishment and severe wrath, and His vengeance on those who associated partners with Him, disobeyed His command, and denied His messengers. "He said, 'O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not then fear Him?'" That is, do you not fear God for associating partners with Him? The leaders, who were the nobles and great ones among them, said, This is only a man like you who wants to do you a favor. They mean to be haughty towards you and to show off by claiming prophethood, while he is a man like you. So how could revelation be given to him and not to you? And if God had willed, He would have sent down angels. That is, if He had wanted to send a prophet, He would have sent an angel from Himself, and he was not a man. We have not heard of this, that is, of the sending of humans among our forefathers, meaning by this their ancestors and grandfathers in past ages. And his saying: He is only a man possessed by madness, meaning he is crazy in what he claims that God sent him to you and chose him from among you for revelation. So wait for him for a time, meaning wait for the vicissitudes of fate to come upon him, and be patient with him for a period until you are relieved of him.

23:26: God Almighty tells us about Noah, peace be upon him, that he called upon his Lord to grant him victory over his people, as God Almighty said, informing us about him in another verse: So he called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, I am overcome, so grant me victory.’ And he said here: My Lord, grant me victory because they have denied me. Then God Almighty ordered him to build the ship, perfect it, and to carry in it two of each kind, meaning a male and a female of every kind of animal, plant, fruit, and other things, and to carry in it his family except for those against whom the word has already gone forth from them, meaning those against whom the word from God has already gone forth to destroy, and they are those of his family who did not believe in him, such as his son and his wife, and God knows best. And His statement: “And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged. Indeed, they are to be drowned.” That is, when you witness the sending down of the great rain, do not be moved by compassion for your people and pity for them, or by the hope of delaying them so that they may believe, for I have decreed that they will be drowned despite their disbelief and transgression. The story has been presented in detail in Surat Hud, so there is no need to repeat it here. And His statement: So when you and those with you have boarded the ship, say, ‘Praise be to God, Who has saved us from the wrongdoing people.’ Just as He said: “And He has made for you of the ship and the grazing livestock wherein you ride, that you may mount on their backs. Then remember the favor of your Lord when you are boarded therein and say, ‘Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, for we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.’” And Noah, peace be upon him, complied with this, as God Almighty said: And he said, ‘Embark therein, in the name of God is its course and its anchorage.’ So God Almighty mentioned it at the beginning of his journey and at its end, and God Almighty said: And say, ‘My Lord, alight me at a blessed landing place, for You are the best to alight.’ And His statement: Indeed in that are signs means that in this action, which is the salvation of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers, there are signs, that is, clear arguments and evidence of the truthfulness of the prophets in what they brought from God Almighty, and that He Almighty does whatever He wills, is capable of all things, and knows all things. And His statement: And indeed We are to test means to test the servants by sending messengers.

23:31: The Almighty informs us that He created another generation after the people of Noah. It was said that what is meant by them is Aad, for they were successors after them. It was also said that what is meant by these is Thamud, because of His saying: Then the shriek seized them in truth. And that the Almighty sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, so he called them to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, but they denied him and disobeyed him and refused to follow him because he was a human being like them. They disdained following a human Messenger, and they denied meeting God on the Day of Resurrection and denied the bodily resurrection and said: Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones you will be brought forth? Far, far is that which you are promised. That is, far, far is that. He is only a man who has fabricated a lie against God. That is, in what he brought to you of the message, warning, and report of the Resurrection. And we are not believers in him. He said, My Lord, support me in that which they deny. That is, the Messenger sought victory over them and sought victory from his Lord over them, so He answered his prayer. He said, ‘In a little while they will surely become regretful.’ That is, in disobeying you. And your stubbornness in what you have brought them, So the blast seized them in truth, meaning, they deserved that from God due to their disbelief and tyranny. It appears that a blast combined with a strong, cold, violent wind destroyed everything by the command of their Lord, so that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. And His statement, So We made them scum, meaning, fallen and destroyed like the scum of a flood, which is a lowly, insignificant, perishable thing that is of no benefit. So away with the wrongdoing people, like His statement, And We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers, meaning, due to their disbelief, stubbornness, and opposition to the Messenger of God. So let the listeners beware of belying their Messenger.

23:45: God Almighty tells us that He sent His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, and his brother Aaron to Pharaoh and his people with the signs, conclusive arguments, and decisive proofs, and that Pharaoh and his people were too arrogant to follow them and submit to their command because they were human beings, just as the previous nations denied the sending of human messengers. Their hearts were alike, so God destroyed Pharaoh and his people, and drowned them all in one day. He sent down to Moses the Book, which is the Torah, in which are His rulings, commands, and prohibitions. This was after God had broken Pharaoh and the Copts and seized them with the grip of the Almighty, the Powerful. After God sent down the Torah, He did not destroy a nation in general, but rather He commanded the believers to fight the disbelievers, as God Almighty said: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations, as insight for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded.
